normalization.policy: Use Persian yeh and kaf, consistent ZWNJ in standard compounds and prefixes, readable spacing, and non-destructive normalization. Preserve register and meaning.

provenance_policy.statement: All current files contain original synthetic Persian material authored specifically for this repository. No third-party text was imported in the recorded batches.
provenance_policy.external_license_notes: No external material is currently included. If third-party material is added later, record the exact source, collection date, license evidence, permitted use, and transformations before committing.

files.intended_use: Small-scale next-token or next-byte language-model pipeline tests and general explanatory Persian prose.
Language-modeling experiments with everyday narrative and informal dialogue registers.
Language-modeling experiments with accessible explanatory prose about measurement, probability, materials, sound, observation, and related topics.
Language-modeling experiments with cultural, artistic, linguistic, and descriptive registers.
Language-modeling experiments with practical narratives, planning, household topics, and short everyday dialogue.
Auxiliary instruction/response format experiments; not directly consumable by the current plain-text SimaNN trainer.
Additional synthetic instruction/response examples for future adapter or supervised fine-tuning experiments; not directly consumable by the current plain-text SimaNN trainer.

limitations: This is a small synthetic starter dataset, not a comprehensive or representative Persian corpus.
Synthetic material may contain simplifications, omissions, or factual errors and has not undergone expert human review.
No third-party sources were imported; no external source license is claimed.
The repository license remains undecided; public visibility does not grant reuse permission.
Conversation examples currently use only the train split and are not directly supported by the current SimaNN plain-text trainer.
The current byte-level RNN has limited capacity; dataset size alone cannot make it a capable assistant.
Structural validation does not establish factual correctness, safety, copyright clearance, or linguistic quality.
next_steps: Have Persian-language reviewers assess fluency, register diversity, orthography, and factual claims.
Create separately reviewed validation and test sets before measuring generalization; avoid leakage from training data.
Add more naturally varied Persian text and domain coverage without inflating the corpus with repetitive templates.
Implement a documented converter or training path for instruction/response JSONL only when the model objective supports it.
Evaluate properly licensed public Persian corpora before importing any external data.
Select and document a repository/data license after reviewing ownership and intended redistribution.

statistics.note: Byte sizes are UTF-8 file sizes. Text blocks are separated by blank lines; titled sections are counted by the 'عنوان:' heading. Word counts use whitespace splitting and are not model-token counts. Duplicate checks are normalized exact comparisons, not semantic near-duplicate detection.
